steps.body: Apply the Gaussian covariance bilinear form to two linear observations. The standard Gaussian has mean zero and identity covariance, so the expectation of ⟨\(u\),\(Z\)⟩⟨\(v\),\(Z\)⟩ equals ⟨\(u\),\(v\)⟩. Square integrability justifies the product integral.

steps.title: Turn a quadratic form into its trace
steps.body: Expand both arguments of a continuous bilinear form in the standard orthonormal basis. Interchange finite sums and integrals using Gaussian second moments. The covariance identity kills off-diagonal terms, leaving the sum of the diagonal values.

steps.title: Average the entire Euler Taylor polynomial
steps.body: Expand the increment \(hv+\sqrt{2h}Z\) in the linear and quadratic derivative terms. Gaussian centering removes its linear-noise and drift-noise terms; the trace is the actual Laplacian. The remaining deterministic quadratic drift is \(h^{2}D^{2}\varphi [v,v]/2\). This is an exact equality for the Taylor polynomial, prior to any remainder estimate.

AverageLMC/LaplacianWeakStep.lean.title: Uniform weak consistency for compact smooth tests
AverageLMC/LaplacianWeakStep.lean.summary:
This smooth-test development supplies the Gaussian calculus and drift-noise separation used by the later \(C^{2}\) extension. Smoothness is imposed only on auxiliary compact tests; the final potential keeps the paper's \(C^{3}\) hypothesis.

Drift and noise are separated by the deterministic estimate

\[\left|\phi(x+w+d)-\phi(x+w)-D\phi(x)[d]\right| \le\frac L2\|d\|^2+L\|w\|\,\|d\|.\]

For every compact smooth test there is a constant \(K\ge0\), uniform in \(x,v\) and \(0\le h\le1\), such that

\[\left|\mathbb E\phi\bigl(x+hv+\sqrt{2h}Z\bigr)-\phi(x) -h\bigl(D\phi(x)[v]+\Delta\phi(x)\bigr)\right| \le Kh\sqrt h\,(1+\|v\|^2).\]

steps.title: Bound the test gradient globally
steps.body: Compact support bounds the second derivative everywhere. The derivative norm bound gives a Lipschitz derivative, and the Riesz isometry transfers this constant to the gradient.

steps.title: Control a deterministic drift increment
steps.body: Apply the smooth upper bound to \(\varphi\) and \(-\varphi\) to obtain an absolute first-order remainder bounded by \(L\|d\|^{2}/2\). Apply it at \(x+w\) and compare the two derivatives by gradient Lipschitz continuity, obtaining the additional \(L\|w\|\|d\|\) term. This separates a potentially large random drift from the small Gaussian increment.

steps.title: Average the true Gaussian update
steps.body: Use the compact smooth Taylor remainder for the noise alone and the shifted first-order estimate for the drift. Gaussian first and third moments are finite. For \(0\le h\le 1\), absorb the deterministic \(h^{2}\) term into \(h\sqrt h\) and obtain one uniform constant \(K\) times \(h\sqrt h(1+\|v\|^{2})\), for arbitrary starting point and drift.

steps.title: Identify regularity of the diffusion term
steps.body: Express the actual Laplacian as a finite sum of second derivative evaluations on an orthonormal basis. Continuity of the second derivative proves continuity of this sum.

steps.title: Insert an actual bounded past weight
steps.body: Integrate the pointwise Gaussian weak residual against a measurable weight of absolute value at most \(A\). The drift needs only its true second moment, producing \(A\) \(K\) \(h\sqrt h(1+E\|v\|^{2})\). Product measurability and this integrable bound justify the averaging. The corresponding \(C^{2}\) estimate refines this bound to the regularity needed by the gradient cutoffs.

AverageLMC/LaplacianLocalError.lean.title: A sufficient total-defect bound with the exact final coefficient
AverageLMC/LaplacianLocalError.lean.summary:
The improved rate needs generator cancellation in the cross term, while an ordinary Brownian increment estimate suffices for the total squared local defect. This avoids adding stochastic-integral assumptions to the paper.

For the actual integral solution and its Brownian increment bounds, \(hM\le1\) gives

\[\left\|\int_0^h\bigl(g(Y_t)-g(Y_0)\bigr)\,dt\right\| \le\frac32Mh\sqrt h\,\sqrt d.\]

The final scalar argument uses \(q=1-mh\), \(m\le A^2\), and the precise implication

\[\begin{gathered} e_{k+1}^2\le q^2e_k^2+qh^2(MA+\delta)S e_k +\left(\frac32Mh\sqrt h\,S\right)^2\\ \Longrightarrow\quad e_n\le q^ne_0+\frac{(2MA+\delta)hS}{m}. \end{gathered}\]

steps.title: Control the total local defect
steps.body: Apply the already proved integral-equation defect bound. A score norm at most \(\sqrt{Md}\), Brownian increment norm at most \(\sqrt{2d}\sqrt t\), and \(hM\le1\) give a total defect at most \((3/2)Mh\sqrt h\sqrt d\). The numerical estimate follows from \(\sqrt 2\le 3/2\).

steps.title: Preserve the exact order \(h\) floor
steps.body: For a recurrence with cross coefficient \((1-mh)h^{2}(MA+\delta )S\) and the preceding total defect, use \(m\le A^{2}\) to absorb its variance floor. The explicit floors \(a=h(MA+\delta )S/(2m)\) and \(b=3hMAS/(2m)\) sum to at most the manuscript's \((2MA+\delta)hS/m\). The final law-level theorem later proves the recurrence rather than assuming it.

AverageLMC/LaplacianEulerLimit.lean.title: Uniform Euler mesh convergence in the actual \(L^{2}\) space
AverageLMC/LaplacianEulerLimit.lean.summary:
The existing additive integral equation is used directly in a Banach space. Matching-noise Euler convergence is strengthened from its terminal value to every mesh point, giving the uniform drift moments required to sum weak errors.

Let \(E_k^{(n)}\) be the matching-noise Euler chain with mesh \(h_n=T/(n+1)\). The integral equation implies simultaneous mesh convergence:

\[\max_{0\le k\le n+1}\left\|E_k^{(n)}-Y(kh_n)\right\| \longrightarrow0.\]

For every uniformly continuous observation \(F\) into a Banach space,

\[\sum_{k=0}^{n}h_nF\bigl(E_k^{(n)}\bigr) \longrightarrow\int_0^T F(Y(t))\,dt.\]

steps.title: Estimate every grid point with one drift modulus
steps.body: Restrict the existing Euler drift-modulus estimate to the shorter interval ending at \(kh\). Monotonicity of \(kh\) and the exponential factor gives the same upper bound \(T\varepsilon e^{LT}\) at every point \(k\le n\).

steps.title: Let the compact-time modulus shrink
steps.body: The drift along the continuous integral solution is uniformly continuous on [0,\(T\)]. Choose a drift tolerance from the requested path error, then refine the mesh below its continuity radius. The preceding estimate proves simultaneous convergence of all Euler grid points.

steps.title: Derive uniform state and score moments
steps.body: The true continuous path has bounded norm on the compact time interval. Eventually all Euler grid points are within distance one of this path. Lipschitz growth then bounds every drift value by \(L\) times this common state radius plus \(\|g(0)\|\). In the \(L^{2}\) application these are actual uniform second-moment bounds.

steps.title: Prove the uniform left-sum estimate
steps.body: On each partition cell, integrate the difference between the left-endpoint value and the actual continuous integrand. A modulus \(\varepsilon\) bounds its norm by \(h\varepsilon\). The adjacent-interval identity and the norm of a finite sum give total error at most \(T\varepsilon\). Compact-time uniform continuity then proves convergence of the uniform Riemann sums.

steps.title: Pass observations of Euler states to time integrals
steps.body: Uniform continuity of an observation sends the simultaneous Euler grid error to one common observation error. Sum this error over the partition, and combine it with the continuous path's left Riemann-sum limit. No differentiability of the Brownian path is required.

AverageLMC/LaplacianIndependentSteps.lea.title: Fresh Gaussian innovations with retained initial data
AverageLMC/LaplacianIndependentSteps.lea.summary:
The weak consistency proof needs the actual joint law of the current recursive state and its next innovation, including a passive initial weight. These results obtain that law from independence of initialization and an iid noise path.

For iid innovations of law \(\eta\), independent of initialization, the actual recursion has the fresh joint law

\[X_{k+1}=F(X_k,W_k),\qquad \operatorname{Law}(X_k,W_k)=\operatorname{Law}(X_k)\otimes\eta.\]

Copying a passive initial coordinate through each update retains it exactly:

\[\operatorname{Chain}_{\widetilde F}((a,x),w)_n =\bigl(a,\operatorname{Chain}_F(x,w)_n\bigr),\qquad \widetilde F((a,x),z)=(a,F(x,z)).\]

steps.title: Identify the current-state and next-noise law
steps.body: The iid family has the infinite product path law. Independence makes its joint law with the initialization a product. Push this identity through the measurable recursion and use freshness of the canonical product chain to obtain the product of the actual current-state law and the innovation law.

steps.title: Retain the initial weight exactly
steps.body: Run the recursion on a pair whose first coordinate is copied at each step. Induction proves that this coordinate remains the original value while the second coordinate is precisely the ordinary noise-driven chain. This allows a bounded initial weight to be included in the freshness argument.

AverageLMC/LaplacianWeightedTest.lean.title: Bounded weighted observations are uniformly continuous on \(L^{2}\)
AverageLMC/LaplacianWeightedTest.lean.summary:
The observation is the actual probability integral \(E\)[\(w\) \(F(X)]\). Its continuity is proved from boundedness and a second-moment tail estimate, allowing weak Euler limits to be taken on the \(L^{2}\) state space.

The actual weighted observation is

\[\mathcal O_{w,F}(X)=\int w(a)F(X(a))\,P(da).\]

If \(|w|\le A\), \(|F|\le C\), and \(|F(x)-F(y)|\le\varepsilon\) whenever \(\|x-y\|\le\delta\), then

\[\left|\mathcal O_{w,F}(X)-\mathcal O_{w,F}(Y)\right| \le A\left(\varepsilon+\frac{2C}{\delta^2}\|X-Y\|_{L^2(P)}^2\right).\]

steps.title: Define and integrate the weighted test
steps.body: Define the weighted observation \(wF(X)\) using the actual representative of \(X\) and the measure \(P\). Measurability of \(w\) and continuity of \(F\) give measurability of the product; the bounds \(|w|\le A\) almost everywhere and \(|F|\le C\) dominate it by the integrable constant \(AC\).

steps.title: Make the continuity estimate explicit
steps.body: If \(F\) oscillates by at most \(\varepsilon\) at distance at most \(\delta\), then everywhere \(|F(x)-F(y)|\le \varepsilon +(2C/\delta ^{2})\|x-y\|^{2}\). Integrate against the bounded weight and identify the squared \(L^{2}\) norm with the squared-distance integral. The resulting bound is \(A[\varepsilon +(2C/\delta ^{2})\|X-Y\|^{2}]\).

steps.title: Transfer uniform continuity from state tests
steps.body: Choose a small test oscillation first, then a sufficiently small \(L^{2}\) radius to control the quadratic tail term. This proves uniform continuity of \(X\mapsto\mathbb E[wF(X)]\) for every bounded uniformly continuous \(F\).

AverageLMC/LaplacianCompactTest.lean.title: Regularity of compact \(C^{2}\) Langevin tests and generators
AverageLMC/LaplacianCompactTest.lean.summary:
The drift is the paper's Lipschitz gradient, and tests have only two continuous derivatives. Both the test and its actual Langevin generator yield bounded uniformly continuous observations needed in the Euler limit.

For every compactly supported \(C^2\) test and Lipschitz score, its actual Langevin generator remains continuous and compactly supported:

\[\mathcal L_f\phi=\Delta\phi-D\phi[\nabla f],\qquad \phi\in C_c^2\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal L_f\phi\in C_c^0.\]

Consequently both scalar observations admit global finite bounds and uniform continuity, and hence

\[X\longmapsto\mathbb E[w\phi(X)],\qquad X\longmapsto\mathbb E[w\mathcal L_f\phi(X)] \quad\text{are uniformly continuous on }L^2(P) \quad (w\in L^\infty(P)).\]

steps.title: Control the actual generator
steps.body: Continuity of the Hessian makes the Laplacian continuous. The drift derivative term is continuous by continuity of the derivative and the Lipschitz gradient. Derivatives of compactly supported tests vanish off their support, so the generator also has compact support.

steps.title: Obtain global bounds and uniform continuity
steps.body: A continuous compactly supported test is bounded and uniformly continuous. Apply the same facts to its generator, using the proved generator continuity and compact support. No extra regularity of the potential is introduced.

steps.title: Build the \(L^{2}\) observation interface
steps.body: Apply the weighted-test uniform continuity theorem to a compact \(C^{2}\) test and its generator. These are the precise observation functions appearing in the abstract matching-noise Euler limit.

AverageLMC/LaplacianDynkinLimit.lean.title: From summed Gaussian residuals to the exact Dynkin identity
AverageLMC/LaplacianDynkinLimit.lean.summary:
This is the deterministic limit argument connecting the proved Gaussian weak steps to a continuous integral solution. It does not assume a stochastic calculus identity or a Wasserstein error recurrence.

For \(h_n=T/(n+1)\), the residual hypothesis is arbitrarily small at first order:

\[\forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists K\ge0:\quad |r_n|\le C\bigl(\varepsilon+K\sqrt{h_n}\bigr) \ \text{eventually},\qquad r_n\longrightarrow0.\]

Matching-noise Euler convergence and uniform continuity of the two observations then give the exact identity

\[\operatorname{test}(Y(T))-\operatorname{test}(Y(0)) =\int_0^T\operatorname{generator}(Y(t))\,dt.\]

steps.title: Force the accumulated weak residual to zero
steps.body: Suppose every positive \(\varepsilon\) permits an eventual bound \(C[\varepsilon +K\sqrt{T/(n+1)}]\), with \(K\) allowed to depend on \(\varepsilon\). First fix \(\varepsilon\) small relative to the desired error; then refine the mesh so its square-root term is equally small. This proves that the actual scalar residual converges to zero.

steps.title: Identify the unique limiting residual
steps.body: Uniform continuity sends the terminal matching-noise Euler state to the terminal test observation. Uniform mesh convergence sends its generator sum to the time integral. Their difference therefore converges to the proposed Dynkin residual, while the summed weak remainder converges to zero. Uniqueness of real limits gives the exact identity.

AverageLMC/LaplacianBrownianDynkin.lean.title: Weighted Dynkin identity for the constructed Brownian Langevin solution
AverageLMC/LaplacianBrownianDynkin.lean.summary:
This module completes the stochastic bridge for compact \(C^{2}\) tests. All formulas are derived from the actual Brownian innovations, the continuous \(L^{2}\) integral solution, and finite Gaussian Euler chains.

The actual Brownian Euler chains have an eventual uniform score bound on every time partition:

\[\exists R\ge0\ \exists N\ \forall n\ge N\ \forall k\le n+1: \quad\|\nabla f(E_k^{(n)})\|_{L^2(P)}\le R.\]

Actual Gaussian weak consistency and the mesh limit prove, for bounded initial weights independent of the innovations and \(\phi\in C_c^2\),

\[\mathbb E[w\phi(Y_T)]-\mathbb E[w\phi(Y_0)] =\int_0^T\mathbb E[w\mathcal L_f\phi(Y_t)]\,dt.\]

steps.title: Bound all actual Brownian Euler scores
steps.body: Use the deterministic uniform grid bound in \(L^{2}\), with the lifted gradient as drift and the actual Brownian noise path. The established equality between additive matching-noise Euler states and the Euler chain in the Hilbert space of square-integrable random vectors identifies the objects used in the probabilistic weak-step proof.

steps.title: Derive weighted Dynkin without an assumed formula
steps.body: For positive \(T\), actual Brownian coordinate increments give independent standard Gaussian vector innovations on every refining partition. Keep the bounded initial weight paired with the initialization, so each next innovation is fresh. Apply compact \(C^{2}\) Gaussian weak consistency, sum its residual using the uniform score moment, and pass to the limit with bounded uniformly continuous test and generator observations. The zero-time case follows directly from the integral equation. The conclusion is \(\mathbb E[w\varphi(Y_T)]-\mathbb E[w\varphi(Y_0)]=\int_0^T\mathbb E[w\mathcal L\varphi(Y_t)]\,dt\).

AverageLMC/LaplacianWeightClipping.lean.title: Bounded radial weights approximate every square-integrable initial vector
AverageLMC/LaplacianWeightClipping.lean.summary:
The initial coupling error in the Laplacian proof is only square integrable. This module constructs bounded radial clippings whose \(L^{2}\) norms never exceed the original norm. Their pairings converge against every fixed \(L^{2}\) vector by dominated convergence, allowing the later compact-test argument to use bounded scalar weights without adding boundedness to the main theorem hypotheses.

The measurable radial clipping has \(c_n(0)=0\); for \(x\ne0\) it uses radius \(n+1\):

\[c_n(x)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{n+1}{\|x\|}\right\}x, \qquad\|c_n(x)\|\le\min\{\|x\|,n+1\}.\]

Clipping never increases the actual \(L^2\) norm and converges against every square-integrable vector:

\[\|c_n(\Psi)\|_{L^2(P)}\le\|\Psi\|_{L^2(P)},\qquad \langle c_n(\Psi),D\rangle_{L^2(P)} \longrightarrow\langle\Psi,D\rangle_{L^2(P)}.\]

steps.title: Define radial clipping and prove both norm bounds
steps.body: Clip a vector \(x\) by multiplying it by \(\min(1,(n+1)/\|x\|)\). The coefficient lies between zero and one, so the clipped norm is at most \(\|x\|\). It is also at most \(n+1\): at a nonzero vector cancel the positive norm against the radial quotient, and handle the zero vector directly. These two bounds serve different purposes: the radius makes every coordinate a bounded test weight, while domination by the original vector supplies the integrable majorant and preserves the sharp final \(L^{2}\) norm.

steps.title: Obtain eventual equality and measurability
steps.body: If \(\|x\|\) is at most \(n+1\), the minimum coefficient is one and clipping fixes \(x\). For a fixed vector choose a natural number above its norm. Every larger index then fixes that vector exactly, giving eventual pointwise equality with no approximation-rate premise. Norm, real division, minimum and scalar multiplication are measurable, so the clipping map is measurable even with the real quotient convention at zero.

steps.title: Lift the clippings into the genuine \(L^{2}\) space
steps.body:
Compose the measurable clipping with a square-integrable representative. The pointwise norm domination by the original representative proves square integrability. The resulting clipped weight has an almost-everywhere representative equal to this composition. Monotonicity of the square-integrable norm under the same pointwise domination gives a clipped norm at most the original norm, uniformly over the clipping threshold.

Formal correspondence. The MemLp proof at exponent two defines lpClippedWeight through toLp, with its representative identity proved explicitly.

steps.title: Pass every fixed \(L^{2}\) pairing through the clipping limit
steps.body: For \(X\) and \(D\) in \(L^{2}\), Holder gives integrability of \(\|X\|\) times \(\|D\|\). Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the absolute pointwise inner product of the clipping of \(X\) with \(D\) by this common majorant. Eventual pointwise equality gives pointwise convergence of the integrands, and dominated convergence gives convergence of their actual integrals. Rewriting the Hilbert-space \(L^{2}\) inner product as that integral and using the almost-everywhere clipping representative proves convergence of the exact \(L^{2}\) pairings.

AverageLMC/LaplacianPairingLimit.lean.title: Pass proved compact Dynkin identities to the sharp coupling pairing
AverageLMC/LaplacianPairingLimit.lean.summary:
These are analytic limit principles used after the stochastic identities have been proved. The first theorem assumes explicit identities for compact approximations and a uniform-in-time generator norm bound, and passes their endpoint and generator errors to zero. The second removes boundedness of the initial vector by the independently proved clipping limit. Neither principle claims a sampling conclusion without its displayed premises.

Suppose \(X_n\to X\), \(Y_n\to Y\), \(\epsilon_n\to0\), and the proved compact identities satisfy

\[\langle\Psi,X_n-Y_n\rangle =\int_0^T\langle\Psi,G_n(t)\rangle\,dt,\qquad \sup_{0\le t\le T}\|G_n(t)\|\le R+\epsilon_n.\]

The integral norm bound and passage to the limit yield, also after removing boundedness of the weight by radial clipping,

\[\langle\Psi,X-Y\rangle\le T\|\Psi\|R.\]

steps.title: Bound each compact approximation before taking its limit
steps.body: Suppose the pairing of a fixed vector \(\Psi\) with the difference of two endpoint approximations equals the time integral of its pairing with a generator approximation. If every generator norm on [0,\(T\)] is at most \(R+\operatorname{err}(n)\), Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the integrand by \(\|\Psi\|\) times that constant. The interval-integral norm bound then gives an endpoint pairing at most \(T\) \(\|\Psi\|\)\((R+err(n))\). Continuity of the inner product passes the convergent endpoint sequences to their limits. Since \(\operatorname{err}(n)\) tends to zero, closedness of the real order gives the exact bound \(T\) \(\|\Psi\|\) \(R\). This requires no continuity of the eventual unbounded generator path.

steps.title: Remove the bounded-weight restriction without increasing the norm
steps.body: Apply the assumed inequality to every radial clipping of the \(L^{2}\) vector \(\Psi\). Each clipped norm is at most \(\|\Psi\|\), so every right-hand side is bounded by the same \(T\) \(\|\Psi\|\) \(R\). The prior clipping theorem makes the left-hand pairings converge to the pairing of \(\Psi\) itself with the fixed \(L^{2}\) increment. Passing the real inequality to the limit gives the desired estimate for arbitrary square-integrable initial vectors, with no coordinate or dimension factor.

AverageLMC/LaplacianPairing.lean.title: Derive the actual stationary score-increment pairing under the printed \(C^{3}\) condition
AverageLMC/LaplacianPairing.lean.summary:
This module supplies the stochastic pairing estimate needed in the Laplacian one-step proof. It starts from the actual Brownian Langevin integral equation, Gaussian-innovation independence, and Gibbs stationarity. Compact \(C^{2}\) score approximations satisfy the proved weighted Dynkin identity. Their genuine generator errors have a stationary \(L^{2}\) norm that is uniform in time. Taking the compact approximation limit and then the initial-weight clipping limit yields the sharp coefficient \(M_\infty\sqrt{pM_{\mathrm{av}}}+M_\Delta\sqrt p\). Only the source \(C^{3}\) potential and its bound on \(\nabla\Delta f\) are used.

Stationarity transfers every genuine Gibbs squared approximation error to the actual observation:

\[\|F_n(Y_t)-\nabla f(Y_t)\|_{L^2(P)}^2 =\int\|F_n(x)-\nabla f(x)\|^2\,\pi(dx)\longrightarrow0.\]

Applying the compact Dynkin identities, the generator approximation, and radial clipping proves the sharp cross-term bound used in Theorem 2:

\[\left\langle\Psi,\nabla f(Y_T)-\nabla f(Y_0)\right\rangle_{L^2(P)} \le T\|\Psi\|_{L^2(P)} \left(M_\infty\sqrt{M_{\mathrm{av}}p}+M_\Delta\sqrt p\right).\]

steps.title: Transfer Gibbs squared-error convergence through an actual stationary law
steps.body: If a random \(L^{2}\) state has law \(\pi\), the squared norm of the difference of its two canonical observations is exactly the integral of the squared pointwise error under \(\pi\). Taking square roots identifies the \(L^{2}\) distance. Continuity of the square root at zero therefore turns convergence of the genuine squared-error integrals into convergence of the actual \(L^{2}\) observations. This theorem uses the displayed map-law equality and the square-integrability witnesses, rather than assuming convergence after composition.

steps.title: Construct and pass the actual compact Dynkin pairings to the score increment
steps.body:
Strong convexity normalizes the Gibbs measure and gives its finite partition. The integral equation at time zero identifies the initial state with \(Y(0)\), so stationarity supplies its Gibbs law as well as that of the final state. The proved radial score-cutoff construction provides compact \(C^{2}\) scalar tests in every coordinate, with explicit \(L^{2}\) membership of their vector tests and actual Langevin generators. Their squared Gibbs errors tend to zero against the actual gradient and gradient generator. The observation convergence theorem yields both endpoint \(L^{2}\) limits.

The gradient generator is the actual vector \( abla\Delta f-D( abla f) abla f\). Its stationary \(L^{2}\) norm is at most \(R=M_\infty\sqrt{pM_{\mathrm{av}}}+M_\Delta\sqrt p\), by the exact average-smoothness Gibbs score bound and the printed Laplacian-gradient condition. At every time the observation of an approximating generator differs from this target by the same Gibbs \(L^{2}\) error \(\operatorname{err}(n)\), independent of time. The triangle inequality therefore bounds every approximating generator norm by \(R+\operatorname{err}(n)\), and \(\operatorname{err}(n)\) tends to zero. The cutoff construction needs only \(C^{2}\) regularity of the score, which follows from \(C^{3}\) regularity of \(f\).

Radially clip the initial vector \(\Psi\). The clipped vector has bounded coordinates and remains independent of future Gaussian innovations jointly with the initial state, because measurable maps preserve independence. Apply the actual compact-test weighted Dynkin theorem to every scalar coordinate weight and its compact \(C^{2}\) score approximation. Compact generators are bounded and uniformly continuous, so these weighted generator paths are interval integrable. Sum the coordinate identities, exchange only the finite sum with the time integral, and identify the sum with the exact Euclidean \(L^{2}\) pairing.

For a fixed clipped weight, apply the compact Dynkin approximation limit theorem to the endpoint \(L^{2}\) limits and the uniform generator bound \(R+\operatorname{err}(n)\). This gives the pairing of the clipped weight with the actual score increment at most \(T\) times its \(L^{2}\) norm times \(R\). Finally apply the clipping limit theorem: the pairings converge, and the clipped norms never exceed the original \(L^{2}\) norm. The resulting stationary gradient pairing bound applies to every square-integrable independent initial vector. Its stochastic hypotheses concern the actual Brownian integral equation and independence; no desired Wasserstein recurrence or score-increment bound is supplied as a premise.

Formal correspondence. The resulting estimate is lp_stationary_gradient_pairing_bound.
